valuation.method: Distributable earnings (DE) per common share x P/E, using FY2027 DE/share as an investor would price it at the 12-month target date (Nov 2027). Reported anchors: Q3 2026 DE $1.32/share (Q3 2025 $1.52), FRE $1.57bn ($1.26/share), net realizations $331.5m, quarterly dividend $1.12 (Blackstone Q3 2026 8-K/10-Q). The FY2027 DE/share inputs are my own model assumptions, not company guidance and not sourced analyst estimates; realizations are the swing factor. USD listing, no FX conversion.

bear.driver: Realizations stay depressed and fundraising slows; FRE growth stalls (private-markets stress, rates stay high)

base.driver: FRE grows high single digits on private-wealth inflows ($63bn Q3 inflows); realizations recover modestly from Q3 trough

bull.driver: Realizations rebound strongly as exit markets reopen, plus FRE growth and multiple re-rating

valuation.implied_by_close: At base DE of $5.60 the $110.80 close implies 19.8x; the two named analyst targets ($122, $127; mean $124.50, null horizon so unweighted) imply 22.2x on the same EPS, or DE of about $5.66 at 22x
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $5.60 (5.1 pp of the close); $0.50 of DE moves it by $11.00 at 22x
valuation.watch_metric: Net realizations and fee-related earnings per share (Q3 2026: $331.5m and $1.26), which drive whether run-rate DE reaches about $5.60
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 2026 results, expected late January 2027 (date not confirmed)

analyst_notes: Only two named analysts (Wells Fargo's Daniel Welden, Goldman's Alexander Blostein) could be verified with dated calls, so the sample is thin and both are Hold. Both predate the Q3 earnings release on 2026-10-22, and neither horizon is documented, so they stay out of the weighted target. Search snippets also showed unverified Oct 2026 target moves (JPMorgan cut, TD Cowen trim, UBS $118, Morgan Stanley Overweight $165) that I could not confirm; web fetch of broker and aggregator pages was blocked. Yahoo's published aggregate (23 analysts, mean $139.04) sits above the base case of $123.2, a gap of $15.8, or about $0.72 of DE at 22x.
